condition: AAA and lung cancer screening — man aged 65–75 who has smoked
permutationLabel: Man aged 68, 30 pack-years, quit 10 years ago
summary: 68-year-old ex-smoker (30 pack-years, quit 10 years ago) at a wellness visit, no symptoms. USPSTF 2019: one-time ultrasound for AAA; USPSTF 2021: annual low-dose CT chest.

inputs.hpi: Asymptomatic 68-year-old retired mechanic at a wellness visit. Smoked 30 pack-years, quit 10 years ago. Treated hypertension. No abdominal or back pain, no cough or haemoptysis. Colonoscopy 4 years ago normal. Never had an aortic scan or chest CT.
inputs.socialHistory: Retired mechanic. Ex-smoker: 30 pack-years, stopped 10 years ago.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for lung cancer
guideline.section: Annual low-dose CT for adults 50–80 with a ≥ 20 pack-year history who currently smoke or quit within the past 15 years (grade B)
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for lung cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2021;325:962–970.

rationale: Men 65–75 who have ever smoked benefit from a single aortic ultrasound; the same smoking history qualifies for lung cancer screening. Both are one-line prompts that are easy to miss in a surgical clinic.
